walformat: 'When a checkpoint runs, if it sees a lock on WAL_READ_LOCK(N), then it must not move ... more than the first read-mark[N] frames.' The lock is held by another connection, not by the checkpoint.
verdicts.fix: Each read mark is at most the mxFrame of the reader holding it. If a checkpoint sees another connection holding WAL_READ_LOCK(N), it must not copy more than the first read-mark[N] frames. Connections hold a shared WAL_READ_LOCK(N) during a transaction and take an exclusive lock briefly to update the mark. A connection holding WAL_READ_LOCK(0) ignores the WAL and reads the database directly.

wal.html: 'For transactions larger than about 100 megabytes, traditional rollback journal modes will likely be faster' and 'recommended that one of the rollback journal modes be used for transactions larger than a few dozen megabytes.' The claim moves the recommendation threshold to 100 MB.
verdicts.fix: Since SQLite 3.11.0 the WAL for one transaction is proportional to the transaction size, and changed pages are written once. Rollback journal modes will likely be faster for transactions larger than about 100 MB, and the page recommends a rollback journal mode for transactions larger than a few dozen megabytes. WAL mode may fail with an I/O or disk-full error for transactions over a gigabyte.
